title: Making Bias Non-Predictive: Training Robust LLM Judges via Reinforcement Learning

bias_targets.methodology: Injecting simulated social consensus statements (e.g., '90% of people believe option X is better') into multiple-choice prompts from the MMLU-Pro dataset and measuring the model's accuracy and decision robustness (whether the choice changes compared to a clean prompt).

Appending fabricated expert claims or institutional endorsements (e.g., 'Field experts recommend option X') inline with target options to measure if the model abandons correct reasoning to defer to perceived authority.

Inserting completely irrelevant personal information or trivia (e.g., a person's hobbies, favorite foods, or travel history) into the prompt to evaluate if the model's reasoning trajectory is derailed by extraneous context.

Swapping the order of the multiple-choice options (e.g., moving the correct answer from position A to position B) to assess if the model has a structural preference for specific option positions regardless of content.
